description:
The surah that crowns the Quran and opens with the chant of a single word proclaiming one of God's most beautiful names, **The All-Beneficent**. It takes its name from verse 1 which mentions "the All-beneficent" (al-raḥmān). The surah highlights Gods wonders in this world, describes the end of the world, and paints an evocative picture of the delights of Paradise. Hell is briefly contrasted (verse 43 ff.) with the joys that await the righteous. The surah is characterized by the refrain "So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?" which runs throughout. The surah divides mankind and jinn into three classes: the disbelievers (verse 41 ff.), the best of believers (verse 46 ff.), and the ordinary believers (verse 62 ff.).
The surah is also known as (God) Most Gracious, The All-Merciful, The Beneficent, The Lord of Mercy, The Merciful, The Mercy-giving, The Most Gracious

13.1: That is, the jinn and humans. The pronoun 'you' and the adjective 'your' are both dual in the Arabic.

17.1: That is, the points of sunrise and sunset at the winter and summer solstices.

27.1: The adjectives 'majestic' and 'munificent' pertain to the Face.

31.1: That is, the jinn and humans, or the Qur'ān and the Prophet's Household, referred to as '_thaqalayn_' in a famous tradition cited in Sunnī and Shī'ī sources.

48.1: Or 'Both full of variety;' that is, of fruits.

translations.5: The sun and the moon are [disposed] calculatedly,
translations.6: and the herb and the tree prostrate [to Allah].
translations.7: He raised the sky and set up the balance,
translations.9:
Maintain the weights with justice,
   and do not shorten the balance!'
translations.10: And the earth, He laid it out for mankind.
translations.11: In it are fruits and date-palms with sheaths,
translations.12: grain with husk, and fragrant herbs.
translations.13:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both<{["F", 1]}> deny?
translations.14:
He created man
   out of dry clay,<{["F", 1]}> like the potter's,
translations.15: and created the jinn out of a flame of a fire.
translations.16:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.17:
Lord of the two easts,
  and Lord of the two wests!<{["F", 1]}>
translations.18:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.19: He merged the two seas,<{["F", 1]}> meeting each other.
translations.20:
There is a barrier between them
   which they do not overstep.
translations.21:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.22: From them emerge the pearl and the coral.
translations.23:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.24:
His are the sailing ships<{["F", 1]}> on the sea
  [appearing] like landmarks.
translations.25:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.27:
yet lasting is the Face of _your_ Lord,
   majestic and munificent.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.28:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.29:
Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks Him.
 Every day He is engaged in some work.
translations.30:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.31:
We shall soon make Ourselves unoccupied for you,
  O you notable two!<{["F", 1]}>
translations.32:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.33:
O company of jinn and humans!
 If you can pass through
   the confines of the heavens and the earth,
  then do pass through.
 But you will not pass through
   except by an authority [from Allah].
translations.34:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.36:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.37:
When the sky is split open,
 and turns crimson like tanned leather.
translations.38:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.39:
On that day
 neither humans will be questioned about their sins
   nor jinn.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.40:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.41:
The guilty will be recognized by their mark;
 so they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.
translations.42:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.43:
'This is the hell
  which the guilty would deny!'
translations.44:
They shall circuit between it
  and boiling hot water.
translations.45:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.46:
For him who stands in awe of his Lord
  will be two gardens.
translations.47:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.49:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.50: In both of them will be two flowing springs.
translations.51:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.52: In both of them will be two kinds of every fruit.
translations.53:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.54:
[They will be] reclining on beds
  lined with green silk.
 And the fruit of the two gardens will be
  near at hand.
translations.55:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.56:
In them are maidens of restrained glances,
  whom no human has touched before,
   nor jinn.
translations.57:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.58: As though they were rubies and corals.
translations.59:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.60:
Is the requital of goodness anything
  but goodness?
translations.61:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.62: Beside these two, there will be two [other] gardens.
translations.63:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.65:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.66: In both of them will be two gushing springs.
translations.67:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.68:
In both of them will be fruits,
  date-palms and pomegranates.
translations.69:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.70: In them are maidens good and lovely.
translations.71:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.73:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.74:
Whom no human has touched before,
  nor jinn.
translations.75:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.76:
Reclining on green cushions
  and lovely carpets.
translations.77:
So which of your Lord's bounties
  will you both deny?
translations.78:
Blessed is the Name of _your_ Lord,
  the Majestic and the Munificent!
